sweep_summary: sanj1284 is not in the catalog. The sweep turned up two Glottolog title-hits that are one and the same work: Chávez Peón's 2010 UBC dissertation on Quiaviní Zapotec prosody (Glottolog 575961 and duplicate 605100). It was already on file from the earlier audit pass at (PDF with text layer; no scanned needed) and I read chapter 3 in full. It is a first-hand, fieldwork-based statement: stress is culminative and demarcative, falling on the root-final syllable (affixes and clitics never stressed; second root in compounds; last syllable of polysyllabic loan roots, with <10 loanword exceptions), analysed as quantity-sensitive moraic trochees with ALIGN-R to the root; duration is the main acoustic cue. It cites Munro & Lopez (1999) for the earlier generalisation 'the last syllable of uninflected words is stressed'. The same author's CLA 2008 proceedings paper (also on file, p.2 and p.13) repeats the last-syllable-of-uninflected-words statement and supplies the acoustic evidence. Nothing new was fetched sources; no items remain unread, so no acquisition priorities. Appended a dated sweep note with verified page locators to in that directory. If the language is added to the catalog, Chávez Peón 2010 p.78/p.101 is the deciding source: fixed root-final (surface: final) stress.

new_statements.quote: [p.74] In Quiaviní Zapotec, neither prefixes nor suffixes are ever stressed. In addition, affixes are never as complex, prosodically and segmentally, as prominent (root) syllables. ... examples with the diminutive suffix and clitics demonstrate that stress is not simply word-final; in these examples, stress is still located on the root syllable ... [p.78] Quiaviní Zapotec shows culminativity in that there is only one prominent syllable per word, and demarcativity in that the (final) root syllable is always prominent. [p.101] In disyllabic and longer words, Quiaviní Zapotec displays a trochaic metrical pattern at the moraic and syllabic level. Further, in accordance with Munro and Lopez (1999), stress is demarcative, with the root-final syllable consistently carrying prominence.

new_statements.rule_in_words: One stress per (content) word, on the final syllable of the root: native roots are mostly monosyllabic, so stress is word-final in prefix+root words and in etymologically opaque or borrowed polysyllables (last syllable of uninflected words = Munro & Lopez's 'key syllable'), but the diminutive suffix and enclitics are unstressed, so stress is root-final rather than word-final; in compounds the last root is stressed. Formalised as ALIGN(Hd(Ft), R, Root, R) with quantity-sensitive moraic trochees; the stressed syllable must be bimoraic (vowel lengthening before lenis coda/open syllable, fortis codas moraic). Main acoustic correlate is duration (Chávez-Peón 2008).
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; culminative single prominence per word. Function words (articles, clitics, some adverbs) 'do not need to be stressed' and are prosodically dependent on content words (p. 49).
new_statements.exceptions: Diminutive suffix -eʔ and clitics never stressed (stress stays on root: [ˈla.teʔ] 'little can', p. 74/84); loanwords keep the Spanish stressed syllable as the prominent syllable and delete post-tonic final open-syllable vowels so that the head is root-final (p. 94-95); tone contours, diphthongs and non-modal phonation restricted to stressed (root) syllables. Note the Teotitlán del Valle variety (Uchihara & Gutiérrez 2020: 15) instead places accent on the last syllable of the phonological word including the diminutive suffix.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the prosodic word = content word (root plus affixes/clitics); examples are citation forms of nouns, verbs, adjectives; the 2008 CLA study measured target words in carrier sentences. Language is tonal (4 tones) with contrastive phonation; stress is independent of tone (tonal-with-stress-statement would also apply, but the location rule is root-final).
new_statements.identity_note: The primary statement (Chávez Peón 2010, 2008; Uchihara & Pérez Báez 2016) describes San Lucas Quiaviní Zapotec, a Tlacolula Valley variety that Glottolog 1's dialect list on file). Uchihara & Gutiérrez 2020 describes Teotitlán del Valle Zapotec (Glottolog dialect teot1238 under sanj1284) and differs in one detail: there the accent falls on the last syllable of the phonological word including the diminutive suffix (bεˈl:εˀn 'little fish'), whereas in Quiaviní the diminutive suffix and clitics are unstressed and stress stays on the root-final syllable ([ˈla.teʔ] 'little can'). Knudson & Jones 1977 (not reachable) describes San Juan Guelavía (sanj1289).

new_statements.reading: Word stress in (San Lucas Quiaviní) Western Tlacolula Valley Zapotec is morphologically fixed on the final syllable of the root: one stress per word; prefixes, suffixes and enclitics never carry it; in compounds it falls on the second (final) root; polysyllabic loan roots are stressed on their last syllable because Spanish post-tonic final vowels are deleted, with fewer than ten lexical exceptions where the Spanish stressed syllable stays non-final. Since native roots are almost all monosyllabic, the surface pattern is 'stress on the root (= last syllable of uninflected words, Munro & Lopez 1999)'. Foot structure is analysed as quantity-sensitive moraic trochees aligned to the right edge of the root (ALIGN-R); duration is the main acoustic correlate. Classification-wise: fixed stress on the root-final syllable (morphologically conditioned, not phonologically word-final).

sources.note: Ch.3 'Metrical structure of Quiaviní Zapotec': stress is culminative and demarcative, the root-final syllable is always prominent; prefixes, suffixes (diminutive) and clitics never stressed; etymologically opaque polysyllables and loanwords have prominence on the last (root) syllable; formalised as ALIGN(Hd(Ft),R,Root,R) with moraic trochees; main acoustic correlate duration (pp. 48, 74, 78, 85, 95, 101).
